## Preliminary & unvetted analysis
Exploratory analysis. The comparison between datasets is observational: designs with and without
non-vanilla trials differ in lab, stimuli, age range and procedure.
:::





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)
i_am("notebooks/03-within.qmd")
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

d <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "vanilla_trials_design.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(session_design == "mixed", !is.na(long_window_accuracy)) |>
  mutate(log_age = log(age),
         prop_prev_nonvanilla = if_else(n_prev > 0, n_prev_nonvanilla / n_prev, NA),
         prev = if_else(prev_nonvanilla, "after non-vanilla", "after vanilla"))
d$log_age_s <- scale(d$log_age)[, 1]
d$log_trial_s <- scale(log(d$n_prev + 1))[, 1]
```
:::





The between-study comparison in @sec-split is confounded with lab, stimuli and age. A cleaner
test uses only the mixed sessions and asks whether a vanilla trial goes worse when it follows
non-vanilla trials, holding trial position constant. If children become unsure what the task is
after odd trials, then:

* a vanilla trial directly after a non-vanilla trial should be less accurate than one after
  another vanilla trial (a local effect), and
* a vanilla trial with more non-vanilla trials before it should be less accurate than one at the
  same position with fewer (a cumulative effect), and
* sessions with a larger share of non-vanilla trials should have lower vanilla accuracy
  (a dose effect across sessions).

This is 23536 vanilla trials from 2700 mixed sessions in
16 datasets.

## Local effect: the trial just before





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
d |> filter(!is.na(prev)) |>
  mutate(pos_bin = floor(n_prev / 5) * 5 + 3) |>
  group_by(pos_bin, prev) |>
  summarise(n = n(), acc = mean(long_window_accuracy),
            se = sd(long_window_accuracy) / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pos_bin, y = acc, colour = prev)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = acc - 1.96 * se, ymax = acc + 1.96 * se),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 1.5)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, lty = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("after non-vanilla" = "#D95F02", "after vanilla" = "#1B9E77"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Trial position in session", y = "Proportion target looking")
```

```{.r .cell-code}
types <- read_csv(here("metadata", "nonvanilla_types.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
by_ds <- d |> filter(!is.na(prev_nonvanilla)) |>
  group_by(dataset_name) |>
  filter(sum(prev_nonvanilla) >= 50, sum(!prev_nonvanilla) >= 50) |>
  group_modify(~ {
    f <- if (n_distinct(.x$age) > 5) long_window_accuracy ~ prev_nonvanilla + log(n_prev + 1) + log_age
         else long_window_accuracy ~ prev_nonvanilla + log(n_prev + 1)
    broom::tidy(lm(f, data = .x), conf.int = TRUE) |> filter(term == "prev_nonvanillaTRUE") |>
      mutate(n = nrow(.x))
  }) |> ungroup() |>
  left_join(types, by = "dataset_name")
ggplot(by_ds, aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(dataset_name, estimate), colour = nonvanilla_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Non-vanilla trials") +
  labs(x = "Coefficient for preceding trial non-vanilla (vs vanilla)\non proportion target looking, adjusting for trial position and age", y = NULL)
```

## Models





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ctrl <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
dm <- filter(d, !is.na(prev_nonvanilla))
dm$prop_prev_c <- dm$prop_prev_nonvanilla - mean(dm$prop_prev_nonvanilla)
dm$prop_session_c <- dm$prop_nonvanilla_session - mean(dm$prop_nonvanilla_session)

mods <- list(
  "local" = lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_age_s + log_trial_s + prev_nonvanilla +
                   (log_age_s | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id), data = dm, control = ctrl),
  "local + cumulative" = lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_age_s + log_trial_s + prev_nonvanilla +
                   prop_prev_c + (log_age_s | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id),
                 data = dm, control = ctrl),
  "local x age" = lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_age_s * prev_nonvanilla + log_trial_s +
                   (log_age_s | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id), data = dm, control = ctrl),
  "session dose" = lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_age_s + log_trial_s + prop_session_c +
                   (log_age_s | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id), data = dm, control = ctrl)
)
est <- imap_dfr(mods, ~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |> mutate(model = .y)) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  transmute(model, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
```
:::

::: {#tbl-within .cell tbl-cap='Within-mixed-session models of vanilla-trial accuracy (proportion scale). `prev_nonvanilla`: preceding trial was non-vanilla. `prop_prev_c`: share of all preceding trials that were non-vanilla (centred; coefficient is the difference between 0% and 100%). `prop_session_c`: share of the whole session that was non-vanilla.'}

## Local effect by type of non-vanilla trial

The hypothesis is most specific for odd-sounding labels, so we let the local effect differ by the
kind of non-vanilla trial the dataset has.





::: {#tbl-local-type .cell tbl-cap='Effect of the preceding trial being non-vanilla, by the dataset\'s type of non-vanilla trial (simple effects from one model with a type x preceding-trial interaction, adjusting for log age and trial position; dataset random age slopes and child intercepts).'}

```{.r .cell-code}
dm <- dm |> left_join(types |> select(dataset_name, type = nonvanilla_type), by = "dataset_name")
local_type <- lmer(long_window_accuracy ~ log_age_s + log_trial_s + type + type:prev_nonvanilla +
                     (log_age_s | dataset_name) + (1 | subject_id), data = dm, control = ctrl)
local_type_est <- tidy(local_type, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "prev_nonvanilla")) |>
  transmute(type = str_remove_all(term, "^type|:prev_nonvanillaTRUE"),
            estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  left_join(dm |> group_by(type) |>
              summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_name), trials = n(),
                        `trials after non-vanilla` = sum(prev_nonvanilla)), by = "type")
knitr::kable(local_type_est, digits = 3)
```

## Summary

* Pooled over all mixed sessions, a vanilla trial directly after a non-vanilla trial is no less
  accurate than one after a vanilla trial
  (+0.005 [-0.003, 0.013]).
* There is no cumulative cost either: at a given position, having had a larger share of
  non-vanilla trials so far goes with slightly *higher* accuracy.
* The session-dose coefficient is large and positive, but the share of non-vanilla trials varies
  almost entirely between datasets and visits, so it carries the same confounds as @sec-split.
* The one place the sign matches the hypothesis is the two mispronunciation datasets
  (swingley_aslin_2002 and moore_bergelson_2022_verb), where accuracy is lower after a
  mispronounced trial in both
  (pooled -0.032 [-0.066, 0.002]).
  That is two datasets and under a thousand trials, the interval reaches zero, and trial order is confounded with items. It is a
  lead, not a finding.

Caveats:

* Trial order within a session was fixed or drawn from a few lists in most studies, so "after a
  non-vanilla trial" is partly confounded with which item was tested.
* Blocked designs (teaching block then test block) contribute little to the local contrast.
* Trials that were never imported into Peekbank are not counted.
